SMTO-GWT-0014 — The Gateway is handling too many requests right now

GUID: f11e2b1e-577d-42bf-8837-1d2d61d0811a
Slug: gateway-nonce-capacity
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • For safety, the Gateway keeps a short list of every request from the last couple of minutes. That list is full, so it refused this request without running it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait about two minutes before trying again. Entries on the Gateway's list drop off after about two minutes, which frees space.
  2. Let some tasks on this Gateway finish, or stop ones you don't need, before starting more. Many tasks running at once send a large number of requests very quickly.
  3. If many scheduled tasks start at the same moment on this Gateway, spread their start times out. Staggered starts keep the request count under the Gateway's limit.
  4. Then run the task once. Don't click repeatedly while you wait. Each extra attempt adds another request to the full list.

What success looks like

  • The task starts on that Gateway without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't delete files on the Gateway computer to clear the list; they protect against repeated requests.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's replay-protection store reached its capacity of retained and pending request nonces after expired records were removed, so authentication refused the request before dispatch.

What this means

  • The count of retained and pending authenticated request nonces reached the replay-protection capacity after expired records were removed. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The count of retained and pending authenticated request nonces reached the replay-protection capacity after expired records were removed.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect request volume and nonce capacity; distinguish this admission failure from a job or storage capacity failure.

How to fix it

  • Retained plus pending nonces reached NONCE_CAPACITY (16384) within the NONCE_TTL window (125 s, gateway_core/client_auth.py). Reduce the request rate to this Gateway (concurrent runs, polling or scheduled bursts) and wait for records to expire; do not delete unexpired nonce records.
  • Allow existing nonce records to expire and reduce request bursts before reconnecting.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Normal request volume fits after nonce expiry and authentication succeeds without deleting unexpired replay evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not use a rapid retry loop or replay an uncertain mutation while waiting for the stated condition.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
